gp.heading: Cost of Revenues and Gross Margin
gp.text: Cost of revenues increased by 49% to $67.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $45.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Cost of revenues increased by 47% to $136.9 million for the six months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $93.3 million for the six months ended September 30, 2025. Gross margin was 28% and 27% for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to 31% and 33% for the three and six months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Cost of revenues includes total amortization expense of $0.5 million and $1.0 million in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, as a result of Comtrafo acquired backlog intangible assets. In addition, $0.7 million related to a fair value adjustment for the step-up basis assigned to acquired inventory to properly reflect the fair value in purchase accounting was charged to cost of revenues in the six months ended September 30, 2026. The decrease in gross margins in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026 was due to a less favorable product mix and the impact of Comtrafo purchase accounting items.

oi.heading: Operating income (loss)
oi.text:
Our operating income (loss) is summarized as follows (in thousands):

Our Grid business segment generated operating losses of $0.2 million and $2.3 million in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026 , respectively, compared to operating income of $1.3 million and $5.4 million in the three and six months ended September 30, 2025 , respectively. The decrease in the Grid business segment operating income in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026 was due to lower gross margins and Comtrafo purchase accounting expense.

Our Wind business segment generated operating income of $4.2 million and $8.1 million in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026 , compared to operating income of $1.7 million and $3.2 million in the three and six months ended September 30, 2025 , respectively. The increase in the Wind business segment operating income in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026 was due to higher revenues and gross margins from increased sales of ECS units.

rd.heading: Research and development
rd.text: Research and development ("R&D") expense increased 1% in the three months ended September 30, 2026, to $3.8 million from $3.7 million in the three months ended September 30, 2025. R&D expenses decreased 4% in the six months ended September 30, 2026, to $7.7 million from $8.0 million in the six months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in the three months ended September 30, 2026 was driven primarily by additional stock based compensation. The decrease in the six months ended September 30, 2026 was driven primarily by lower total compensation expense.

ga.text: Selling, general and administrative ("SG&A") expenses increased 36% in the three months ended September 30, 2026, to $18.3 million from $13.4 million in the three months ended September 30, 2025. SG&A expenses increased 34% in the six months ended September 30, 2026 to $36.9 million from $27.6 million in the six months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in SG&A expense in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026 was driven primarily by the addition of Comtrafo expenses, higher total compensation expense, and additional stock-based compensation expense.

sga.text: Selling, general and administrative ("SG&A") expenses increased 36% in the three months ended September 30, 2026, to $18.3 million from $13.4 million in the three months ended September 30, 2025. SG&A expenses increased 34% in the six months ended September 30, 2026 to $36.9 million from $27.6 million in the six months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in SG&A expense in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026 was driven primarily by the addition of Comtrafo expenses, higher total compensation expense, and additional stock-based compensation expense.

pretax.text: We define non-GAAP net income as net income before stock-based compensation, amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, change in fair value of contingent consideration, and other non-cash or unusual charges. We believe non-GAAP net income assists management and investors in comparing our performance across reporting periods on a consistent basis by excluding these non-cash charges and other items that we do not believe are indicative of our core operating performance. In addition, we use non-GAAP net income as a factor to evaluate the effectiveness of our business strategies. tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income tax expense was $3.4 million and $4.7 million in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to income tax expense of $0.1 million and $0.3 million in the three and six months ended September 30, 2025 , respectively. The increase in our income tax expense was primarily due to the existence of a valuation allowance against our net U.S. deferred tax assets in the prior year, a majority of which was released during the three months ended December 31, 2025, and taxes in foreign operations in the current year.

net.heading: Net income
net.text: Net income was $3.0 million and $12.5 million in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $4.8 million and $11.5 million in the three and six months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The decrease in net income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was driven primarily by additional tax expense. The increase in net income for the six months ended September 30, 2026 was driven primarily by the change in fair value of contingent consideration.

ocf.text: The Company’s primary sources of liquidity are internally generated cash provided by operating activities, our cash and cash equivalents on hand, along with access to capital markets, including through our currently effective Registration Statements on Form S-3. We believe that these sources of liquidity are sufficient to meet both our short-term and reasonably foreseeable long-term requirements and obligations. As of September 30, 2026, we had cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash of $181.9 million, compared to $147.6 million as of March 31, 2026, an increase of $34.3 million. As of September 30, 2026, we had $24.0 million in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash in foreign bank accounts. capex.text: We believe we have sufficient available liquidity to fund our operations and capital expenditures for at least the next twelve months and into the future. We may seek to raise additional capital, which could be in the form of loans, convertible debt or equity, to fund our operating requirements and capital expenditures. There can be no assurance that we will be able to raise additional capital on favorable terms or at all or execute on any other means of improving our liquidity as described above. Additionally, the impact of global sources of instability, including the ongoing conflicts between Russia and Ukraine and in the Middle East, tariffs, trade restrictions and resulting trade conflicts, instability of financial institutions and political instability in the United States, on the global financial markets may reduce our ability to raise additional capital, if necessary, which could negatively impact our liquidity.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text:
Total revenues increased 43% to $94.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and total revenues increased 36% to $188.1 million for the six months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $65.9 million and $138.2 million for the three and six months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Our revenues are summarized as follows (in thousands):

Our Grid business segment accounted for 82% of total revenues for both the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 83% for both the three and six months ended September 30, 2025. Our Grid business segment revenues increased 41% to $76.7 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $54.3 million in the three months ended September 30, 2025. Our Grid business segment revenues increased 34% to $153.0 million in the six months ended September 30, 2026, from $114.4 million in the six months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in the Grid business segment revenues in the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three and six months ended September 30, 2025, was driven by the addition of Comtrafo revenues along with organic revenue growth.

Our Wind business segment accounted for 18% of total revenues for both the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 17% for both the three and six months ended September 30, 2025.

intro.text: Guided by a belief in the power of next, AMSC is a leading provider of power controls solutions that apply innovation and creativity to address today's challenges and enable a more resilient and sustainable energy future. Driven by the purpose "to power progress," the Company integrates future-facing technologies to balance the global demand for clean energy with reliable, efficient power delivery. AMSC delivers advanced grid systems and engineering services to optimize network reliability, provides ship protection and power management solutions to enhance fleet efficiency and safety, and supplies electronic controls and designs that reduce wind energy costs. Beyond these systems, the Company provides capabilities in industrial process and control alongside environmental and emission control to ensure operational efficiency across the entire energy infrastructure.

s.t: In fiscal 2025, Inox accounted for 15% and Fuji Bridex accounted for 10% of our total revenues.
In fiscal 2024, Inox accounted for 14% of our total revenues.
In fiscal 2023, Inox accounted for 13% of our total revenues.
No other customer accounted for more than 10% of our total revenues in each of fiscal 2025, 2024, and 2023.
In addition, approximately 16% and 7% of our revenues in fiscal 2025 were derived under sales contracts where prices were denominated in the Euro and Real, respectively.
The Grid business segment accounted for 84% of total revenues in both fiscal 2025 and 2024.
Our Wind business segment accounted for 16% of total revenues in both fiscal 2025 and 2024.
For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 , 89 % of revenue was recognized at the point in time when control transferred to the customer, with the remainder being recognized over time.
For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025 , 88 % of revenue was recognized at the point in time when control transferred to the customer, with the remainder being recognized over time.
For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2024 , 80 % of revenue was recognized at the point in time when control transferred to the customer, with the remainder being recognized over time.

This exciting energy future also depends on computer chips, batteries and fuel cells that are built from silicon, lithium and carbon.

We believe that competitive performance in the marketplace depends upon several factors, including technical innovation, range of products and services, product quality and reliability, customer service and technical support.

We rely upon third-party suppliers for the components and subassemblies of many of our Grid and Wind products, making us vulnerable to supply shortages and price fluctuations, which could harm our business.
Many of our components and subassemblies are currently manufactured for us by a limited number of qualified suppliers.

We rely upon the capacity, reliability, and security of information technology hardware and software infrastructure and networks (collectively, "IT Systems"), and our ability to expand and update such IT Systems in response to our changing needs.
We manage certain IT Systems but also rely on IT Systems and various products and services provided by critical third-party vendors and others in the supply chain.

Because we rely on certain third party vendors that support our operations, successful cyberattacks that disrupt or result in unauthorized access to third-party IT Systems can materially impact our operations and financial results.
While we achieved profitable results in fiscal 2025 and 2024, our ability to sustain profitability depends on numerous factors, many of which are outside of our control.

As a result of all of these factors, comparing our operating results on a period-to-period basis may not be meaningful, and you should not rely on our past results as an indication of our future performance.

We have operations in, and depend on sales in, emerging markets, including Latin America and India, and global conditions could negatively affect our operating results or limit our ability to expand our operations outside of these markets.
Our financial performance depends upon our ability to carry on our operations and sell our products in such emerging markets.
The success of our business will also depend on our ability to develop new technologies without infringing or misappropriating the proprietary rights of others.
We rely on trade secrets to protect the majority of our proprietary technologies, especially where we do not believe patent protection is appropriate or obtainable.
We also rely on trade secrets and proprietary know-how to protect our intellectual property.

Our business, like others within the energy technologies industry, is faced with growing cybersecurity threats as we increasingly rely on digital technologies across our business, some of which are managed by third -party service providers on whom we rely to help us collect, host or process information.
The Company’s primary sources of liquidity are internally generated cash provided by operating activities, our cash and cash equivalents on hand, along with access to capital markets.

We have a long history of working with multiple types of projects and preparing cost estimates, and we rely on the expertise of key personnel to prepare what we believe are reasonable best estimates given available facts and circumstances.
